title: First days in New York: meeting Chick Webb, Cozy Cole, Krupa
summary: He met Chick Webb, Cozy Cole, Gene Krupa and young Buddy Rich, and recalls Cozy in a dime-a-dance band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What did you do in New York, once you got to New York?

I come to New York... I was here about, oh, three or four days. I'd go around at night, meet the different musicians. The first one I met was Chick Webb. The next was Cozy Cole. Gene Krupa. I met Buddy Rich, but he was real young then, about seventeen or eighteen years old.
Yeah, he must have been at that time.
Because he played at the Hickory House.

Well, how did these guys impress you at the time, people like Cozy and Chick Webb? Cozy seems to have been a very serious individual about drums and drumming. He was always studying. Was he that way when you first met him?

Yes... Cozy Cole, well, he know more about drums, and he could play. He's got that name, Cozy Cole. When I first met him, he was playing a dime-a-dance on 125th Street; a dance school, a dance hall on 125th Street. He had a five-piece band down there. I went down there... Of course, you couldn't do no settling down there, because that's a dime a dance, and they're playing two... They play about two choruses, and you'd hit on the woodblock, and that's when the girl would take a tip. And when I saw Cozy again, I think he was with Cab Calloway. Then he went over to Blanche Calloway. I think he did something... I'm not sure... No, he didn't do anything with Benny Goodman.
No, unless it was later. But he did at least record with...
I know Big Sid Catlett was with Benny Goodman for a while.
